business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) and Digital Scanning

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (socialist legal system with civil law tradition)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 1 December 2003, effective 11 November 2005)

Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland concerning the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 15 May 1986, effective 6 April 1988)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (revised and adopted 8 November 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities jointly issued by the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024; Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024); Administrative Measures for the Recordation of Beneficial Owners of Non-Financial Payment Institutions and relevant PBOC circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent corporate registration authority of the foreign investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a qualified notary public in the issuing jurisdiction followed by (i) Hague Apostille under the Apostille Convention by the designated competent authority of the issuing state when the destination is also an Apostille Convention state; or (ii) Consular Legalization by the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China located in the issuing jurisdiction when the destination is not an Apostille Convention state. The two paths are mutually exclusive and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent corporate authority in the foreign investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a qualified notary public in the issuing jurisdiction followed by either (i) Hague Apostille by the issuing state's competent authority for use in China (an Apostille member); or (ii) Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate in the issuing jurisdiction for non-Apostille states. No chaining of the two mechanisms is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation and signing of the Sino-foreign Equity Joint Venture
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor, notarized by a local notary public and authenticated by the competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the signature(s) of authorised directors by a local notary, followed by (i) Apostille from the designated authority of the issuing country for Apostille Convention members; or (ii) Consular Legalization through the Chinese consulate for non-members. These procedures are alternatives; they cannot be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and Memorandum of Association of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or notary public in the foreign investor's jurisdiction under the applicable corporate law
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy endorsed by the registry or notary, then either (i) Hague Apostille by the competent authority if the foreign investor's jurisdiction is an Apostille state and the document will be submitted to Chinese authorities; or (ii) Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate in the foreign investor's jurisdiction if the same jurisdiction is not an Apostille member. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial banking institution maintaining the foreign investor's primary operating accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signing by an authorised bank officer with bank seal, then notarization (if required by the issuing country), followed by either (i) Hague Apostille by the issuing country for Apostille Convention states for submission in China; or (ii) Consular Legalization before the Chinese Embassy/Consulate in the issuing country for non-Apostille states. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative and must not be chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all members of the board of directors, the general manager, the supervisor, and all beneficial owners (at or above 25%) against: (i) the PRC joint punishment list for tax evasion and serious violations of trust; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and consolidated non-SDN lists; (iii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; (v) the UK HMT consolidated list; and (vi) applicable domestic and Interpol criminal databases. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined in PBOC Order No. 3 — foreign, domestic and international PEPs and their family members or close associates — trigger enhanced due diligence and require senior management approval. Screening must be repeated at each financing round, on any change of ownership, and at a minimum every 90 days. Any positive hit must be escalated to the JV board and the relevant Chinese financial institution before any contribution of capital.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Autonomous Declaration System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - online portal accepting pre-incorporation name clearance applications and name reservations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory Chinese name of a Sino-foreign equity joint venture must use simplified standard Chinese characters and follow the strict four-tier structure: [Administrative Division Name] + [Selected Unique Name] + [Industry Description] + [Legal Form (e.g., Limited Liability Company)]. A parallel English or pinyin transliteration may be entered as a second registered name, but the primary legal name cannot be in Latin script, Cyrillic, or any non-Chinese script. The selected unique name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing enterprise name or a famous trademark within the same industry. Any name including tokens that imply a state organ, financial institution, or public service must obtain prior written approval from the competent ministry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected or denied name declaration is subject to administrative reconsideration: the applicant or an authorized attorney must file a written appeal with the market regulation authority at the next higher level within 60 days from the date of rejection. The appeal must quote the exact rejection code, demonstrate that the proposed name satisfies the four-tier structure, and include any prior ministerial approval for sensitive tokens. No extension of the 30-day reservation period is available; the applicant may simply file a new declaration after identifying a different unique name. If the higher authority upholds the rejection, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within 6 months from the date of the reconsideration decision or from the expiration of the statutory response period, whichever is later.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole registered address for a Sino-foreign equity joint venture, and is especially rejected for an ISIC 8299 commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) and digital scanning business. Chinese registration, tax (State Taxation Administration) and banking (PBOC) authorities demand a physical operating address evidenced by a lease contract or property certificate, the original registered business license, and the ability to receive official letters. In addition, the enterprise must hold a physical service location under the PRC Postal Law and the Measures for the Administration of Express Delivery before the CMRA licence is granted. A virtual office may be maintained only as a secondary correspondence address for sales and marketing. Banks conducting KYC will refuse to open a corporate account at a purely virtual address. Therefore, the JV must lease or own a physical office in the registered district, put a signboard outdoors, and maintain original accounting and statutory books at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: (1) verify that the lease agreement, property ownership certificate, and current business address in the national enterprise credit system are identical; (2) confirm that a physical signboard with the Chinese legal name is installed; (3) ensure that all original accounting vouchers and paid-in capital verification certificates are stored on site; (4) make certain that a designated financial officer or legal representative is available at the registered address during local business hours; (5) do not use a disconnected residential address or a single suitcase office without staff; and (6) maintain a lease term of at least one year with option to extend. Quantified risk: municipal SAMR and tax authorities conduct risk-targeted spot checks for CMRA entities at an estimated frequency of 15% to 25% in the first two years after incorporation; the risk rises above 40% if the registered address is a shared service office, a common virtual office floor, or a building containing more than 20 registered companies. These inspections are typically initiated without prior notice under the Measures for Administrative Inspection of Enterprise Information Publicity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR enterprise name autonomous declaration and administrative approval
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory registration fee is charged by SAMR for name clearance or company incorporation; the official tariff is zero.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner information filing with PBOC/SAMR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official filing fee is imposed under PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 [2024]; the statutory preserve is zero.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign investor corporate documents - notarization of Certificate of Incorporation, Good Standing, Board Resolution, Articles and Bank Reference Letter (5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public office in the foreign investor's jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notary tariff of USD 150 to USD 200 per document, plus translating notary statements if required.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification for the five notarized corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction (e.g., Secretary of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or competent registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or administrative apostille fee of USD 30 to USD 60 per document at the receiving authority.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of the authenticated corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered translation agency in China (accredited by the local SAMR for foreign-language documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 0.20 to USD 0.30 per Chinese character, typically with a minimum fee of USD 100 per document; estimated at USD 140 per document for five documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC counsel fees for Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence, name clearance, UBO piercing and legalization coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External PRC law firm retained by the JV parties
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing flat-fee market rate for stage 1 pre-incorporation compliance work in Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen or Guangzhou ranging from USD 3,000 to USD 6,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account onboarding and KYC/AML compliance pack preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed PRC law firm or bank compliance consultant assisting with PBOC KYC documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark quote for assembling corporate documents, beneficial owner declarations and account resolution for a commercial bank account.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal engraving (franchise seal, legal representative seal, financial seal and invoice seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government-guided fee of RMB 50 to RMB 100 (USD 7 to USD 14) per seal; four seals totaling approximately USD 40 to USD 50, with safety chip options increasing the price.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical office rent deposit for registered address for three months (refundable if remitted later)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord or leasing company of the physical registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of USD 800 to USD 1,200 per month for a small physical office with meeting room in a second-tier Chinese city; deposit is not a government fee but is a mandatory pre-incorporation expense for commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mail scanning and virtual office software setup, secure mail handling equipment and PMB operation tools
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance technology vendor and CMRA software supplier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market price for a comprehensive CMRA mail scanning platform with audit logs, digital mailbox and recurring billing gateway integration (Stripe) for a new operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 9, 10, 16, 20, 27, 28, 32 and 50; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 28, 29 and 31; and the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Company Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Company together with the Articles of Association, submitted through the SAMR National Integrated Enterprise Registration Online Platform or the local AMR enterprise registration window.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023) there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a general Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture providing ISIC 8299 services. The shareholders determine the registered capital in the Articles of Association and must pay their subscriptions in full within five years from establishment unless a shorter period is set. No blocked escrow account is required by national law for this business scope; foreign shareholders must contribute in a lawful currency through a licensed foreign exchange capital account, and the company may not reduce or withdraw capital except through the statutory capital reduction procedure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [ENTITY NAME] (the Company), adopted by unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting in accordance with the Articles of Association and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. The undersigned directors, comprising a quorum, hereby adopt the following resolutions. 1. Share Capital Subscription: The Directors confirm the registered capital of RMB [AMOUNT], divided into equity interests as set out in the Articles of Association. Each founding shareholder subscription set forth in the contribution schedule is accepted, and the Legal Representative is authorized to open a foreign-invested capital contribution account and to effect all filings necessary to evidence due subscription. 2. Banking Authorization: The [NAME OF BANK] branch is designated as the Company principal bank. The Chairman or General Manager, together with any one of the Chief Financial Officer, the Finance Manager or the Legal Representative, is authorized to open transactional bank accounts, sign account documents, receive deposits, and issue remittance instructions. Banks shall receive a certified copy of this resolution and the specimen signatures of all authorized signatories. 3. Registered Office: The Company registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], and the Directors authorize the execution of the tenancy or serviced-office agreement, payment of rent, and registration of the address as the statutory domicile. 4. Statutory Officers: The Directors appoint [NAME] as Chairman and Legal Representative, [NAME] as General Manager, [NAME] as Supervisor, and [NAME] as Corporate Secretary and Compliance Officer. Such officers shall have all statutory powers and duties under applicable Chinese law, including the implementation of anti-money laundering and sanctions screening procedures and data processing rules for the mail scanning business. 5. Seal and Corporate Governance: The Company adopts the proposed Articles of Association, authorizes the engraving of the Company Seal, Financial Seal, Legal Representative Seal, and Contract Seal, and adopts the internal corporate governance manual covering board meetings, record keeping, conflicts of interest, personal information protection, and business continuity. 6. General Authorization: Any officer is authorized to sign, execute and deliver any agreements, certificates, and filings to the State Administration for Market Regulation, tax authority, social insurance bureau, bank, public security authority, postal authority, or municipal agencies necessary to perfect the incorporation and licenses of the Company. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed in the corporate minute book. Unanimously adopted on [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-approval and Corporate Structure Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration System / local Administration for Market Regulation online window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name and state the intended form as a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture limited liability company. The filing must include the business scope in ISIC 8299 terms, the proposed registered address, the nationalities of shareholders, and the intended capital structure. The system will run duplicate-name checks, prohibited-word checks, and protection-of-well-known-enterprise-name checks. If the name is approved, print and retain the Name Pre-approval Notice. This notice is a precondition for the subsequent formation application and must not be altered after approval.
required_dossiers: Proposed registered address lease intent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant receives a written or portal notice listing conflicting or prohibited elements. The applicant may choose a new name or, if the rejection is based on a substantive objection, submit a written explanation and apply for administrative reconsideration within the applicable limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Notarization and Legalization of Constitution Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chinese Consular Legalization or Apostille authorities in the foreign investor home jurisdiction, Chinese notary offices, and the legal representative signature confirmation office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing, each foreign shareholder must produce its certificate of incorporation or equivalent legal existence evidence, notarized in the home jurisdiction and then legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate or covered by apostille if the jurisdiction is party to the Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalization for Foreign Public Documents. All corporate authorizations, board resolutions, and signatures of the designated legal representative must be authenticated. The Chinese-language articles of association must be signed by all shareholders or their authorized representatives. The notarized documents must be translated into Chinese by a licensed translation service where required, and the original plus translation must be retained for the AMR filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation of each foreign shareholder
Power of attorney for the Chinese filing agent
Passport or ID copies with notarized Chinese translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR considers the foreign documents insufficient, obtain a fresh notarization and legalization cycle or submit a supplementary explanation. Expired legalizations must be reactivated; if the foreign owner refuses, the filing can be refiled after correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Incorporation with the Market Regulation Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Integrated Enterprise Registration Online Platform / local AMR Enterprise Registration Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the online portal and complete the unified application for establishment of a limited liability company. Attach the approved name notice, signed articles of association, lease and property availability documents for the registered office, identity proof of the legal representative, supervisors and officers, the capital contribution schedule, and the declaration of business scope. Submit the foreign-invested enterprise information report at the same time; the platform transmits required data to the commerce department and tax registration system. Upon approval, the AMR issues the Business License with a unified social credit code. This registration constitutes the birth of the company and the legal basis for all subsequent licensing. There is no official state filing fee.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Registered office proof such as lease or serviced-office hosting deed
Identity documents of directors, legal representative, supervisor, and manager
Application for Company Registration signed by all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regulator issues a Correction Notice, the agent must upload correct information within the stated period, usually 10 to 15 calendar days. If the application is cancelled, the applicant may reapply with a new application number once the deficiencies are cured, preserving the name pre-approval if still valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Seal Engraving, Banking and Tax Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving service, local State Taxation Administration branch, social insurance and housing fund offices, and the chosen commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the Business License is issued, have the Company Seal, Financial Seal, Legal Representative Seal, and Contract Seal engraved at an approved engraving service and record the seal specimen with the public security authority. Complete the tax registration information confirmation in the electronic tax bureau within 30 days, and register for general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer status as appropriate. Open the RMB basic deposit account and, if foreign capital will be remitted, a foreign currency capital account at a licensed bank; the board resolution and specimen seals are presented for bank account opening. Enroll the company and its employees in social insurance and housing fund schemes, and execute all labor contracts in writing. The registered office shall, where applicable, complete the office occupancy fire safety filing and obtain occupational safety acceptance for employees.
required_dossiers: Pro Forma Board Resolution appointing bank signatories
Office lease and fire safety filing documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax activation is queried, complete the requested online information or visit the tax service hall with the license and seal. If bank account approval is delayed by KYC or AML reviews, supply updated organizational documents and ownership certifications; if a seal is rejected, order a new seal with a new filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Postal and CMRA License Review and Data Compliance Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Post Bureau of the People's Republic of China and its provincial or mainland postal administrations; local AMR for scope changes; cybersecurity and personal information protection regulators for data processing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the ISIC 8299 virtual office and commercial mail receiving agency, map each element of the service: physical mail reception, scanning, electronic forwarding, storage, and destruction. Define in an operational manual whether the Company transmits documents physically or only digitally. If the Company does not collect, transport or deliver mail or parcels as a postal operator, a postal operating license is not required, but the service scope and charges must match the AMR registration. If physical forwarding by a third-party universal postal service is involved, execute licensed agency contracts with postal operators. Because scanned mail may contain personal data, implement Personal Information Protection Law safeguards: lawful basis, purpose limitation, retention schedules, encryption, access controls, breach notification plan, and a Data Processing Impact Assessment if large-scale or sensitive data are processed. Apply for certification or file the appropriate postal information form if the local postal administration determines that mail agency requires a lightweight filing.
required_dossiers: Operational service manual and privacy policy
Data protection impact assessment where applicable
Anti-money laundering and sanctions screening procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the postal administration asserts that the activity requires a postal or express business license, the Company should suspend any physical forwarding and apply for the requisite license, or amend contracts to delegate all physical delivery to holders of express licenses. For personal information protection queries, revise the privacy policy, appoint a responsible person, and demonstrate lawful processing; administrative correction orders should be cured within the order period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), together with the State Post Bureau of the People's Republic of China for any postal service determinations; the office fire safety authority is the local Fire and Rescue Division.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Enterprise Legal Person Business License is mandatory; a separate Express Delivery Business License is triggered only if the company physically collects, transports, or delivers postal items; pure virtual office and mail scanning services require general commercial registration plus postal-law compliance filing only if required by the local postal administration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity exists under ISIC 8299; the Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China or local Ecology and Environment Bureau has no engagement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the activity is an office-based virtual office, mail scanning and data-processing service; it does not fall under full EIA Report, Environmental Registration, or Exempt categories for industrial projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, VOCs, hazardous waste or combustion emissions are generated; office waste and e-waste must be sorted and collected by licensed municipal waste services according to local city regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office and any mail-handling room must obtain and keep valid fire safety inspection and acceptance clearance from the local Fire and Rescue Division, including emergency exits, extinguishers, smoke alarms and evacuation plans. Workplaces must meet occupational safety requirements with suitable lighting, electrical safety, privacy locks and business continuity provisions. If any storage of paper mail exceeds ordinary office volumes, municipal fire code limits on stored combustibles must be respected.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online electronic portal: National Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax Bureau) accessible through https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn; STA public portal: http://www.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Business License from the provincial Market Supervision Administration; the license bears the 18-digit Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number for PRC enterprises. Step 2: Within 30 days after business license issuance, the legal representative or authorized tax agent must enter the competent STA bureau through the e-Tax Bureau portal and complete the one-time initial tax registration by inputting the USCC, legal entity details, business scope, bank account information, and expected tax types including Corporate Income Tax and VAT. Step 3: The e-Tax system determines whether the entity is a small-scale VAT taxpayer or a general VAT taxpayer; if projected annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000, general VAT taxpayer registration is compulsory. Step 4: After registration, the taxpayer activates electronic invoicing through the STA full digital electronic invoice platform and obtains e-invoicing credentials, encryption keys, and the filing password. Step 5: For a foreign non-resident enterprise with no PRC establishment but earning China-source income, the payer or the non-resident itself must file the non-resident tax registration with the competent STA authority using the cross-border contract, payment schedule, non-residence evidence, and the relevant tax treaty benefit application if a treaty is claimed; the tax authority then assigns a non-resident tax identification code for withholding and filing purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity classification regime and does not provide domestic hybrid mismatch elections. A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is automatically treated as a Chinese resident enterprise taxed at the entity level. The only relevant statutory election is the VAT taxpayer type election: a small-scale VAT taxpayer with annual taxable turnover below RMB 5,000,000 may voluntarily elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer, subject to a 12-month lock-in period after approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales for compulsory general VAT taxpayer registration; there is no minimum threshold for initial tax registration because every enterprise formed under PRC law must register for tax upon incorporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under the STA Golden Tax Phase IV framework, all VAT invoices, including special VAT invoices and ordinary VAT invoices, must be issued through the mandatory Full Digitalized Electronic Invoice (e-Fapiao) platform or STA-approved e-invoice service; each invoice is transmitted in real-time to the STA central fiscal database, which generates the invoice code and anti-counterfeiting digital stamp. Special VAT invoices must include the buyer's Uniform Social Credit Code, and input VAT deduction is allowed only after the STA invoice verification system matches and validates the invoice data. Zero-rated or exempt export service invoices are marked accordingly in the e-Fapiao system, and the invoice data is cross-checked against foreign exchange receipt records during tax refund audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Caishui [2016] No. 36 and subsequent implementing notices, 0% VAT may apply to cross-border taxable services provided by a PRC taxable entity to an overseas unit or individual where the service is wholly consumed outside China. The relevant business process management and offshore service outsourcing categories may cover virtual office and mail scanning services if the service is delivered to a non-resident client, used entirely outside the PRC, and paid for in foreign exchange. The taxpayer must retain evidence of the overseas recipient, the offshore consumption location, service performance outside China, and cross-border remittance. If the service is not within the enumerated zero-rated list, no zero rate applies and the standard 6% VAT on business services is chargeable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable for pure service exports: no Customs Export Declaration or Bill of Lading is required for digital scanning and mail scanning services that do not physically cross the border.
Export service contract with the overseas client clearly identifying the service scope, parties, price, and settlement currency.
Commercial invoice issued through the e-Fapiao system in the name of the overseas client and marked as a zero-rated export service.
Bank foreign exchange receipt slip or collection record from a designated PRC bank evidencing actual cross-border foreign exchange payment from the overseas client.
Service performance evidence showing complete offshore consumption, including digital usage logs, mail scanning delivery records, cloud access records, and the overseas client acceptance certificate.
Business registration file containing the Business License and Uniform Social Credit Code (TIN), together with the VAT general taxpayer qualification certificate.
If incidental physical goods are exported, add the Export Goods Customs Declaration and Bill of Lading to substantiate the goods element.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If a zero-rated export claim is not substantiated, the competent tax authority will reverse the zero rating, reassess output VAT at the standard 6% rate, impose a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the underpaid tax from the original due date, and may impose an administrative fine from 50% to five times the evaded tax under Article 63 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Tax Administration and Collection of Taxes. Cases involving fraudulent invoices, false foreign exchange records, or fabricated export services to obtain VAT refunds are referred for criminal prosecution under the PRC Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refunds, which carries penalties of imprisonment and property confiscation. In addition, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange may impose separate penalties for failure to repatriate or report export proceeds within the prescribed deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange rate system with strict separation between current and capital account foreign-exchange transactions. Current-account items such as trade proceeds, service fees, and dividends are generally freely convertible once substantive background documents are provided, but every transaction must be justified by real commercial or investment activity and entered into the SAFE monitoring system. Capital-account items, including the initial foreign direct investment injection, acquisition of domestic shares, foreign-currency loans, and outward portfolio investments, require prior SAFE registration or approval. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are permissible subject to audited financials, tax clearance, and foreign-exchange registration, but the bank must verify that the entity has fulfilled annual inspection and reserve requirements. Export proceeds are no longer subject to a forced sale ratio; they may be retained in foreign currency accounts or settled at the bank's RMB price, but all funds must be repatriated into China and recorded. During the recent regulatory tightening, banks have also adopted heightened review of fund-source documentation, strict anti-money-laundering procedures, and real-time cross-border matching, turning any mismatch between declared business scope and actual fund flow into a de facto block. For a virtual-office/mail-scanning JV, the lack of physical manufacturing and reliance on intangible digital services amplifies the regulator's concern about shell-entity structures, so capital injections below minimum thresholds and frequent high-volume digital payments will trigger enhanced review rather than a routine KYC pass.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign-currency receipts must be repatriated to a domestic foreign-exchange account within 180 days from the customs export declaration date; proceeds may be retained in foreign currency without mandatory conversion or converted to RMB at the bank's ruling price, but all collection, retention, and settlement details must be reported electronically to SAFE through the bank. Advance receipts or collections beyond 180 days require prior SAFE registration or a bank-level conditional report.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Basic Deposit Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Domestic fintech payment companies in China hold only nonbank payment licenses and cannot lawfully process foreign-exchange domestic transactions for corporate entities. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise and Revolut are not licensed to open local-currency bank accounts or maintain SAFE-registered capital accounts for onshore Chinese legal entities. They may support offshore collection and disbursement ancillary to the JV's operational needs, but cannot substitute for a Tier-1 Chinese bank in receiving registered equity investment, executing SAFE filings, or settling export proceeds. Viability rating: Low for core treasury functions; acceptable only as a supplementary collection rail if contractually permitted and free of local regulatory conflict.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one statutory director or the singly designated legal representative of the JV must appear physically at the bank's branch for identity verification and interview before account activation. Remote opening for a foreign shareholder does not eliminate this requirement; the foreign investor can execute a notarized power of attorney (apostilled or consular-legalized) authorising the domestic director, and supporting corporate documents must be certified or legalized, but video-only KYC will not pass the Chinese account-opening procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-office and mail-scanning services (ISIC 8299 / NAICS 561431) are inherently mail-forwarding-adjacent and raise shell-company, concealment-of-identity, and invoice-mill concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) valid CMRA/PRC business licence with unified social credit code; (2) signed virtual-office premises sublease or service agreement; (3) utility and administrative evidence of physical operation; (4) workflow and client-onboarding AML policy for mail scanning; (5) audit-trail log demonstrating despatch/clearance records and retention of sender-recipient identification; (6) a written business rationale explaining why the JV chooses this commercial model and how it monitors suspicious payers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound cross-border capital from a foreign parent or investor whose ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) is obscured by trust, foundation, or multi-tier holding structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: full corporate registry extracts; an unbroken shareholder/UBO register up to natural persons; audited parent financial statements for the latest 3 years; bank references; a source-of-wealth affidavit; confirmation of the foreign investor's legal existence and tax residence; and a SAFE-registration pre-file showing the investment route matches the capital-escrow instructions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Common-Chinese-name signatories and JV director triggering PEP or negative-media alerts when screened at the global AML threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: national identity card/passport, notarised residential certificate, current curriculum vitae, professional referee letter, a negative-media search file, a signed PEP questionnaire, and a sworn declaration stating whether the individual holds or has held any public-office position; if yes, include details and source-of-funds proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A digital-revenue virtual office model showing projected payment rails (Stripe recurring, credit-card) that are inconsistent with declared mail-scanning fee patterns, thus suggesting layered commingling or third-party payment laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: 12-month cash-flow forecast and billing model; sample client contracts and fee schedule; underlying invoices and receipts for 3 representative transactions; proof of statutory operating licence; an AML manual covering transaction monitoring, travel-rule compliance, and suspicious-transaction reporting; and evidence that payment-rail collections are attributable to genuine client escrow relationships.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor shall wire the subscribed equity through SWIFT MT103 to the JV's designated capital-escrow account at a Tier-1 PRC bank. The remittance instruction must carry the SAFE foreign-exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment inflow (as registered in the JV's bank-ledger code set), a consistent invoice or contract reference, and the payer's beneficial-owner identifier. The receiving bank will immediately match the amount and currency against the entity's FDI registration and may require the original notarised joint-venture contract and capital-verification report before allowing use of funds. Proceeds must be booked into the capital account and settled as RMB only after capital verification by an up-to-date Chinese certified public accountant; settling earlier without bank consent is a compliance violation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and operating-sweep disbursements, use SWIFT MT103 for direct telegraphic transfers on current-account transactions; use irrevocable commercial letters of credit (L/C) opened against sales/purchase contracts for documentary trade; and use documentary collections (D/P or D/A) when a buyer's bank is required to guarantee payment. Each outbound payment must be supported by invoices, bills of lading, contract, customs declaration and tax payment receipts, with the real-transaction background verified under SAFE’s current-account administration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign-exchange contracts with a Chinese-designated bank, executed only against real current-account exposure with underlying trade/contract documents
FX swaps (CNY/USD, CNY/EUR) with onshore banks for liquidity management, limited to genuine export/import cash-flow matching
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put structures) with a domestic bank under a master ISDA/CSA where the JV has balance-sheet capacity to take delivery at maturity

Offshore non-deliverable-forwards (NDFs) in CNH markets may be used for hedging the foreign parent's outside-China exposure, but are not permitted onshore for the PRC entity and must be booked in a non-PRC subsidiary

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report / Annual Publicity Statement under the Market Regulation System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 January to 30 June of the year following the reporting fiscal year; the annual report covers data as of 31 December of the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The enterprise is included in the Operation Abnormal List if it misses the 30 June deadline; if it does not undergo rectification within 3 years, it is moved to the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List and the registration authority may revoke the business license and administratively strike off the enterprise registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (FDI Statistical and Change Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce of the PRC (MOFCOM), reported through the SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System under the integrated annual reporting mechanism
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same annual reporting window: 1 January to 30 June of the following year; separate real-time or 30-day update is triggered by shareholding or beneficial ownership changes during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing, misleading information, or failure to update the foreign investment information report can result in a warning, an order for correction, or an administrative fine of up to RMB 500,000 under foreign investment information reporting rules; the SAMR annual-report abnormal-list process also applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements Audit and Independent CPA Opinion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting and board of directors; audit opinion must support the CIT annual settlement, the SAMR/MOFCOM annual reporting pack where required, and any foreign exchange or dividend remittance application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audited financial statements should be completed before the corporate income tax annual settlement filing deadline of 31 May; internal reporting to shareholders is typically completed within 120 days from the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If a compulsory audit is omitted, the company and its responsible persons may be ordered by SAMR, tax authorities, or financial regulators to correct the omission and may attract fines under the PRC Accounting Law; tax authorities may reject loss carryforwards, tax incentive filings, or annual report approvals until a compliant audit is supplied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Annual Final Settlement and Reconciliation Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration of the PRC through the local tax authority office with jurisdiction over the registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the tax year; the annual return, supporting schedules, and any balance payment are due together; advance quarterly payments are made during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpaid or overdue tax accrues a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, approximately 18.25% per annum; failure to file may attract a late-filing penalty up to RMB 10,000; false or omitted income may be penalized at 50% to 5 times the evaded tax amount, with potential tax-authority freezing of bank accounts, compulsory enforcement, and exit-restriction measures for legal representatives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual Income Tax (IIT) Monthly Withholding Returns and Annual Comprehensive Income Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration of the PRC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding declaration and payment by the 15th day of the following month; resident employees' annual comprehensive income settlement is accepted from 1 March to 30 June after the year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold or file can result in late-filing penalties of up to RMB 10,000, daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and tax-authority enforcement including bank account withholding; no direct corporate strike-off is triggered, but tax delinquency impedes normal-operation certification and administrative services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Social Insurance Contribution Bases or Average Wage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau / Social Insurance Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by a date notified by the local social insurance agency, typically 31 May or 30 June following the contribution-base year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare the annual wage base exposes the employer to assessed or imputed contribution bases, late fees calculated daily on overdue contributions, administrative fines for underpayment, and civil enforcement; persistent serious violations can affect bidding, financing, and senior management movement but do not directly strike off the corporate registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent PRC-certified CPA audit is compulsory for: (1) all Sino-foreign equity joint ventures regardless of size, pursuant to the PRC Company Law and the PRC Certified Public Accountants Law; (2) any enterprise with total assets greater than RMB 50 million, annual operating revenue greater than RMB 50 million, or more than 200 employees; (3) any enterprise classified as medium-sized or large under the applicable SME classification for commercial business services; (4) any enterprise carrying forward a CIT loss, filing a tax loss-offset, engaging in related-party transactions, enjoying tax incentives, applying for foreign exchange FDI repatriation, or participating in M&A or restructuring; and (5) any licensed commercial mail receiving agency required by local public security, banking, or anti-money-laundering licensing conditions to present audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS / PRC GAAP), which are substantially converged with IFRS; small and micro enterprises may apply the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises only if they do not exceed the audit thresholds and have no listing or regulatory disclosure obligations; where the joint venture has a foreign parent, consolidated reporting should be reconciled to IFRS or home-country GAAP for the parent consolidation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China has no public UBO registry. Beneficial ownership information is collected under AML rules through financial institution customer due diligence processes and through the annual foreign investment information report. Every year by 30 June, the Sino-foreign JV must confirm controlling shareholders, actual controllers, and ultimate beneficial owners in its integrated SAMR/MOFCOM annual report. Any shareholding transfer, share pledge, or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the shareholders' register and filed with SAMR within 30 days of the change; the company must also update its UBO records supporting the PBOC CDD obligations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Senior Management
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board of Directors Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 2,500 per year for a compliant virtual office registered address with mail scanning and agent representation in first-tier cities; USD 500 to USD 1,500 in secondary cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to USD 12,000 for a small or medium Sino-foreign JV with CMRA mail scanning operations; USD 15,000 to USD 30,000 if a consolidated, IFRS, or group audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE) if qualified; reduced rate of 20% (effective 5%-10% on taxable income brackets) for Small Low-Profit Enterprises meeting statutory thresholds; R&D expenses eligible for 100% additional deduction; potentially preferential treatment in designated pilot free trade zones or encouraged industry catalogues; no general patent box regime, but certain technology transfer income may be partially exempt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (Form A200000) and related schedules filed via the State Taxation Administration's electronic tax filing system (电子税务局 / e-Tax portal); the compulsory annual filing package is the 'Annual CIT Return for Resident Enterprises (A-type, 2017 revision)'.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return must be filed and settled within five months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by May 31); quarterly provisional payments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross revenue from principal business, other business operations, and non-operating income, including all domestic and cross-border receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income as a Chinese resident enterprise. For the CMRA/digital scanning business, include subscription fees, mail scanning service fees, virtual office rental income, and any Stripe settlement receipts. Ensure that revenue from non-resident clients sourced through online payment rails is fully declared; failing to include offshore card/bank receipts is a top audit red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income specifically identified by tax law as non-taxable, such as certain government grants and earmarked fiscal subsidies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a virtual office/scanning JV, rarely applicable. Do not treat payments received from foreign clients for mail scanning as non-taxable. If any government digitalization grant is received, verify it falls within the statutory catalogue and document its use strictly; otherwise include in Box 1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary business costs incurred in generating income, including wages, rent, depreciation, software licensing, cloud storage, scanning consumables, and subcontracting fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only costs with valid invoices (Fapiao) and proper substance. Cross-border payments to related parties for software, management, or services must satisfy arm's length pricing and the contemporaneous documentation thresholds. If a non-resident affiliate is paid for 'mail scanning software', the payment may be recharacterized as a royalty or hidden profit distribution if no real service is substantiated; such disallowed expenses increase Box 3 reversals and create WHT exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Line 4): Taxable Income before Losses and Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted to taxable income before applying loss carryforwards, fixed asset deductions, and other special adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile this line to the audited financial statements. The tax authority may apply transfer pricing adjustments if the JV's net margin from mail scanning services falls outside the arm's length range (typically TNMM benchmark for CMRA/business support ISIC 8299). Ensure that any excessive intercompany expenses are added back here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Line 5): Loss Carryforward from Prior Years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses available to offset current-year taxable income, limited to the statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly established JV, this is usually zero. If losses exist, ensure they were filed in prior returns and that the 5-year carryforward limit has not expired. Special 10-year extension applies only to qualifying small enterprises or high-tech enterprises. Cross-border loss usage is not permitted for non-resident branch losses unless treaty rules explicitly provide.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final chargeable income after offsetting losses and applying all special deductions; this is the base for computing CIT at the applicable rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure must match the adjusted net profit attributable to the Chinese JV. A paper-thin or zero taxable income on recurring cross-border digital service revenue, while paying high management or royalty fees to a related offshore entity, is an immediate trigger for Special Tax Audit and GAAR investigation. Maintain a profit level consistent with the functional profile of a routine CMRA/scanning service provider.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10/Box 10: Tax Rate and Tax Payable Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the statutory 25% headline rate or preferential rate to taxable income, and computation of final CIT payable after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If claiming the 15% HNTE rate, attach the valid HNTE certificate and ensure the scanning/software business falls within the encouraged high-tech scope. If claiming small-pro-profit preferential treatment, verify the headcount, asset, and income thresholds. For a JV with non-resident ownership, no deemed dividend reduction applies to the corporate tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for income taxes paid outside China on foreign-source income included in the Chinese taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the JV operates through a foreign branch or earns foreign-source service income, claim a credit only for actual foreign tax paid and limited to the Chinese CIT attributable to that foreign income. Any foreign virtual office arrangement that constitutes a permanent establishment outside China must be disclosed; failure to disclose can lead to double non-taxation penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: RMB 2,000 fixed plus RMB 50 per day of delinquency (capped in practice but escalating with administrative enforcement); late payment interest at 0.05% per day; understatement penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax for fraudulent or negligent misdeclaration; criminal liability for tax evasion exceeding statutory thresholds (e.g., tax underpaid exceeding RMB 500,000 or more than 10% of payable tax) including imprisonment up to 7 years and fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder, unless a double tax treaty reduces the rate (e.g., 5% under the China-Hong Kong DTA for a beneficial owner company holding at least 25% of the shares).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction tax authority; (2) submit the TRC and a beneficial ownership declaration to the Chinese withholding agent before the dividend distribution; (3) provide evidence of substantive business operations, employees, and premises in the residence state, proving the recipient is not a conduit or letterbox entity; (4) show the shareholding meets the minimum holding period and percentage required under the applicable DTA (usually 12 months and 25% for dividends); (5) file the applicable form (e.g., 'Application for Tax Agreement Treatment' or withholding reduction record-filing) with the Chinese tax authority; and (6) maintain all supporting documents for at least 10 years. For Hong Kong treaty relief, the Hong Kong company must demonstrate dedicated business substance in Hong Kong, not merely invoice flows.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest WHT: 10% for non-resident enterprises and 20% for individuals; treaty-reduced rates vary (e.g., 7% under China-Hong Kong DTA for interest, 10% under China-US treaty, etc.). Statutory royalty WHT: 10%; treaty-reduced rates vary (e.g., 5% under China-Hong Kong DTA for royalties, 10% under many others). Royalties include payments for use of or right to use copyrights, patents, software, know-how, and commercial equipment. Payments for cloud software and proprietary scanning algorithms may be treated as royalties; service fees that are not for technology transfer are generally not subject to WHT unless characterized under the 'service PE' rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (Common Local File) is compulsory when related-party controlled transactions in a single fiscal year exceed RMB 40 million (or where intangible property transfers exceed RMB 100 million, or intercompany service fees exceed RMB 40 million); Master File is required when total related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion, intangible transfers exceed RMB 100 million, other controlled transactions exceed RMB 200 million, or the enterprise's cross-border related transactions involving multiple jurisdictions meet the specified threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China imposes substance requirements through the substance-over-form principle under the Enterprise Income Tax Law, General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR), Special Tax Adjustment rules, and beneficial ownership tests under tax treaties. For a CMRA / virtual office mail scanning entity, the Economic Substance Doctrine requires that core income-generating activities (CIGA) — including client contracting, mail reception, scanning operations, data management, and compliance oversight — actually occur in China with adequate staff, premises, and decision-making. A entity that merely passes mail scanning fees through a low-tax jurisdiction or claims treaty benefits without local operational substance may be considered an economic-substance shell, leading to recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, and imposition of dividends WHT.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting cross-border digital service revenue received through Stripe or other payment processors, or creating false invoices/expenses to reduce Chinese taxable profit by shifting income to a non-resident related company without economic substance, thereby causing underpayment of corporate income tax exceeding the criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 63 and 64 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, the taxpayer shall be追缴 (recover) the underpaid tax and pay a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount; under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, tax evasion involving a large amount and high proportion of tax due is punishable by imprisonment up to 7 years, plus a fine of 1-5 times the evaded tax. The tax authority may impose administrative blacklisting on the 'serious dishonest tax defaulter' list, triggering travel bans and restrictions on legal representative's departure from China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil: directors may be personally jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid taxes and penalties if the court pierces the corporate veil due to fraud, abuse of corporate personality, or commingling of personal and corporate assets. Criminal: directors who直接策划 or knowingly participate in tax evasion face imprisonment for up to 7 years and personal fines; the court may order confiscation of personal assets traced to the evasion. Travel: the legal representative and responsible directors are subject to Chinese court 'restriction on exit' (出境限制) and SAT blacklisting, effectively preventing international travel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance & Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Sino-Foreign JV as a pure pass-through or letterbox entity without genuine business activity, using the virtual-office CMRA business as a cover to accumulate Chinese-source income while claiming paper residency in another jurisdiction, and channeling profits to a Hong Kong or offshore intermediary that lacks substance, solely to access reduced DTA withholding rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the GAAR (Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and Implementation Regulations), the tax authority may disregard the entity, recharacterize transactions, deny treaty benefits, impose 10% WHT on deemed dividends, and levy an adjustment penalty of 10%-50% of the additional tax. Under the PRC Company Law and anti-abuse tax provisions, the company's tax registration may be revoked; criminal liability may arise for fraudulent treaty abuse under general fraud or evasion charges. Administrative blacklisting and license revocation by the State Administration for Market Regulation are also possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil: directors who establish or maintain a shell entity to avoid tax may be held personally liable for the tax shortfall and damages to minority shareholders/counterparties; courts may pierce the veil where the entity is found to be a mere instrumentality, and personal assets can be attached to satisfy tax judgments. Criminal: personal involvement in a scheme to abuse a tax treaty and misrepresent beneficial ownership can support charges of fraud or tax evasion, with up to 7 years imprisonment. Travel: blacklisting on the tax authority's 'joint punishment list' imposes restrictions on riding high-speed rail, airplanes, and exiting China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a commercial mail receiving agency and virtual office service without the required postal administrative license, failing to perform customer due diligence, and laundering proceeds of crime by processing payments for illegal mail scanning or virtual office clients through Stripe and credit card rails while deliberately concealing beneficial ownership and transaction trails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Postal Law of the PRC (Articles 52-53) and Implementing Regulations, unlicensed commercial mail receiving/forwarding businesses are subject to fines of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000, confiscation of illegal income, and closure of the business. Under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law, financial intermediaries and designated non-financial institutions failing AML obligations face fines up to RMB 5 million or 5%-10% of the involved transaction amount and suspension/revocation of licenses. If mail scanning is used to launder proceeds, the criminal offense under Article 191 of the Criminal Law (Money Laundering) carries imprisonment from 5 up to 10 years for serious cases, plus forfeiture of illegal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil: directors who knowingly allow unlicensed mail operations or AML deficiencies may be personally liable for regulatory fines and civil compensation to harmed parties; the corporate veil may be pierced on grounds of ultra vires acts. Criminal: a director who directs or clarifies money laundering through the JV's payment infrastructure can be tried as a co-principal and sentenced to 5-10 years in prison, with personal and family assets subject to forfeiture/international freezing. Travel: the court or tax/AML regulators may impose travel bans, and the individual's name is placed on the national 'no-exit' list while under investigation.
